# Pre-retirement Python observations

`observations.json` preserves 570 distinct fixed language inputs observed by the
Python executor at revision `fd1ceb07b2a32e23a90457fe0cfa5dafd69f62a5` before its
removal. These are current-engine retirement observations, separate from the
pinned pre-VM historical corpus under `tests/compatibility/`.

The capture ran 615 existing fixed-case tests, all passing. It wrapped only the
old `_run_python_case` helper, recording that helper's normalized status, return,
writes and events. Expected observations were never generated by the native VM.
The fixture records Python version, selected tests and exact SHA-256 hashes of
the old observer, executor, compiler and runtime. Each source hash was checked
against the recorded Git revision and the unchanged working file before freezing.

The complete fixture SHA-256 is:

`6d8ac0c5fb37b1bea47c6cf7370bf960458cff1bc18088c14c961b5d8acb4d5d`

Inputs and observations use a typed JSON encoding. Addresses hash the complete
input, retaining tuple/list distinctions, dictionary insertion order, exact
float bits (including signed zero), runtime wrapper types and dependencies.
Observations retain builtin sets inside failure arguments. The reader returns a
fresh decoded value for each request, so tests cannot mutate shared expectations.

Maintained tests load these immutable observations without importing or executing
the retired engine. A changed input must receive independent reviewed native
expectations or a new, explicitly provenance-backed historical capture; there is
no automatic expectation update path. Generated stateful sequences instead use
an independent counter/item/claim state machine with exact event/write/rollback
checks in `test_vm_stateful_fuzz.py`.
